stdout.description: Captured stdout, without status messages or placeholders. Empty output is an empty string. May contain only the tail when stdout_truncated is true.

stderr.description: Captured stderr, without tool error messages. Empty output is an empty string. May contain only the tail when stderr_truncated is true.

exit_code.description: Bash exit code after completion; null when not started or still running. Signal termination uses -1 and includes signal.

status.description: Execution lifecycle state. completed means the process ended, not necessarily that it succeeded.

duration_ms.description: Elapsed execution time in milliseconds; zero when not started.

timed_out.description: True when the timeout terminated the process group; false for a command continuing in the background.

cancelled.description: True when request cancellation terminated the process group.

pid.description: Bash process ID, present when a process was started.

signal.description: Termination signal name, present for signal termination.

stdout_bytes.description: Total stdout bytes captured at the time of this snapshot, before tail truncation.

stderr_bytes.description: Total stderr bytes captured at the time of this snapshot, before tail truncation.

stdout_truncated.description: Whether stdout contains only the tail. Limit: 30000 bytes for completed commands, 2000 bytes for background snapshots.

stderr_truncated.description: Whether stderr contains only the tail. Limit: 30000 bytes for completed commands, 2000 bytes for background snapshots.

output_file.description: Retained combined log path for background execution, truncation or a read failure. Includes the final status line when finished.

stdout_file.description: Retained stdout log path for background execution, truncation or a read failure. Contains no status line.

stderr_file.description: Retained stderr log path for background execution, truncation or a read failure. Contains no status line.

error.description: Tool startup, capture or read error. This is not command stderr and may exist even when exit_code is zero.
